LESSON: READING 7.2.1INTENSIVE READING: VISUALS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1Intensive Reading: Visuals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 7.2.1Intensive Reading: Visuals, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why are pictures and photographs important in written texts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 7.2.1Intensive Reading: Visuals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Digital literacy is enhanced as the learner uses digital devices to search for different information conveyed through visuals.

 Citizenship is enhanced as the learner discusses national symbols such as the national flag and currency as examples of

visuals.

66

Values:
Patriotism is enhanced as the learner acquires information about their country while discussing visuals like the national flag and

the Kenyan currency.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Environmental conservation is enhanced as the learner creates visuals such as drawings and realia on natural resources.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of visuals to their learning in other learning areas such as Creative Arts and Sports, Social

Studies, Mathematics and Integrated Science.
